name: Rati Bakradze
medium: Thick acrylic and oil on canvas laid on fast with a broad, rough brush — heavy uneven strokes, dry drags and visible canvas; big flat areas of opaque colour, a few lines scratched or drawn into the wet paint
colour: bright flat colour fields — sky blue, pink, coral red, mustard yellow, grass green and soft grey — with black shapes and small red accents
form: a FEW large, simple, clearly outlined shapes — a person, a black dog, a horse, a bull, a bird — reduced to strong solid silhouettes with almost no detail inside them; people with oversized hands and faces; wide landscapes of two or three flat bands of colour; lots of empty flat ground around the shapes
never: never photographic, never fine detail or shading, never a child's drawing, never cute or cartoonish, never thin wobbly outlines, never many small figures or busy decoration, never patterns filling shapes, never printed text, letters or numbers, never signatures
mood: warm, humorous and a little melancholic
consent: VERBAL agreement — the owner, 2026-09-29 (his standing word: an artist he asks me to add has agreed verbally). A short written agreement (share, credit, withdrawal) is still to be signed before any label is sold.
bio: Rati Bakradze is a Georgian painter. His canvases tell small, funny and tender stories in bold, flat colour — black dogs chasing red balls, horses under huge flowers, people with oversized hands under wide skies — painted with a deliberately childlike, loose hand that turns everyday moments into quiet fables. (Draft biography — to be completed with the artist.)
